search_bias: Autonomous-scientist systems and empirical research-agent papers; strongest quantitative primary sources first, then citation/failure branching. This run started from AI Scientist v2 / Agent Laboratory / AI co-scientist and expanded into 2025-2026 benchmark and audit literature.

checked_sources.title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
The More You Automate, the Less You See: Hidden Pitfalls of AI Scientist Systems
Can AI Conduct Autonomous Scientific Research? Case Studies on Two Real-World Tasks
AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents
AutoResearchBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Complex Scientific Literature Discovery
ResearchClawBench: A Benchmark for End-to-End Autonomous Scientific Research
ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence
PseudoBench: Measuring How Agentic Auto-Research Fuels Pseudoscience
Autodata: An agentic data scientist to create high quality synthetic data

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Full-artifact scientific audit: evaluate trace logs plus generated code, not only the final paper.
evidence: Controlled evaluation of Agent Laboratory and AI Scientist v2 found paper-only pitfall detection around 55% accuracy / 0.51 F1, versus about 82% accuracy / 0.81 F1 when trace logs and code were available.

The same study found strong post-hoc selection bias: Agent Laboratory shifted toward candidates with artificially favorable test results (reported p < 1e-10) and AI Scientist v2 even more strongly (reported p < 1e-30).
Nature's internal audit of the workshop-accepted AI Scientist paper found approximately 57% train-test overlap in a synthetic dataset; the external reviewers did not detect it.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Current open-source AI scientist systems and controlled synthetic/review tasks; strongest evidence concerns detection of methodological failures, not direct improvement of discovery quality.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: The best way to integrate the audit into an online research loop, rather than post-hoc review, remains under-tested.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Best-first / tree-based parallel experimentation rather than one-shot or purely sequential ReAct.
evidence: AIRS-Bench reports that a Greedy tree-based best-first scaffold substantially outperforms ReAct and One-Shot scaffolds as task difficulty increases; reported normalized-score summaries by difficulty are Greedy 0.94/0.82/0.41/0.08 versus ReAct 0.64/0.55/0.12/0.04 and One-Shot 0.36/0.13/0.13/0.01 for easy/medium/hard/expert groups.

The AI Scientist uses staged agentic tree search across initial investigation, hyperparameter tuning, research-agenda execution, and ablations, with best checkpoints carried forward; Nature reports paper quality improves with additional compute.
AI Scientist v2 generated one workshop-level paper scoring 6.33 (6,7,6), but only 1 of 3 submissions cleared the workshop bar and the workshop acceptance rate was about 70%.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: ML research tasks with executable computational experiments. AIRS-Bench provides stronger scaffold evidence than the AI Scientist case study.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need per-model matched scaffold ablations to separate scaffold effect from model/backend and budget effects.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Externalize method selection into an explicit, inspectable methodological-planning stage before execution.
evidence: ASI-Bench evaluates 18 agent-model configurations across 60 project-level tasks and progressively removes human methodological guidance. Mean score falls from 50.91 with full methodological guidance to 29.10 with only the method specified and 26.62 when agents must determine the method themselves.

ResearchClawBench reports strongest autonomous agent score 21.5 with a 50-point target-paper rediscovery threshold; errors concentrate in experimental protocol mismatch, evidence mismatch, and missing scientific core.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Project-level research tasks across multiple scientific domains; evidence diagnoses method-selection/protocol bottlenecks rather than proving a specific planner implementation.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need to identify planning mechanisms that recover the guidance gap without reintroducing human-specific hidden state.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Protocol-to-evidence consistency verifier that checks whether executed experiments actually match the claimed scientific method and whether manuscript claims are backed by logged results.
evidence: ResearchClawBench error analysis localizes failures to experimental protocol mismatch, evidence mismatch, and missing scientific core.
AI Scientist v2 internal reviews found examples of reported experiments not substantiated by execution, code-to-text mismatches, and data-integrity issues.
The Pitfalls study shows full traces/code reveal methodological failures that final-paper review frequently misses.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Verifier architecture hypothesis derived from multiple failure analyses.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: No clean randomized ablation yet found for adding such a verifier to the research loop.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Premise-validity / adversarial-scientific-alignment gate before an autonomous research loop invests in experimentation and writing.
evidence: PseudoBench contains 200 curated pseudoscientific claim-evidence pairs across five domains and tests seven auto-research agents end-to-end.
Reported refusal rates are near zero; hazard is 72.6%-84.6% and the best resistance score is only 27.4%, showing that stronger research agents may polish rather than reject bad premises.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Adversarial pseudoscientific premises; this supports a missing safety/epistemic gate, not a specific gate implementation.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need mitigation studies that preserve legitimate high-risk or contrarian hypothesis exploration while blocking evidence-free premise laundering.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Agentic self-challenging data/task generation with outer-loop meta-optimization of the data-scientist/research-agent recipe.
evidence: Autodata's Agentic Self-Instruct iteratively generates and revises research questions using weak/strong solver discrimination. Reported weak-vs-strong separation expands from about 1.9 percentage points under CoT Self-Instruct to roughly 31-34 points under agentic generation.
On the harder agentic CS test set, reported mean@3 rises from 0.366 (base) to 0.500 after CoT data training and 0.632 after Agentic data training.
Outer-loop meta-optimization raises held-out QA separation pass rate from 62.1% to 79.6% over roughly 233 proposed prompt mutations.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Training/evaluation data creation rather than full autonomous science, but directly demonstrates a transferable meta-optimization loop for improving an agent's own research-task generator.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Transfer to end-to-end scientific method selection, experimentation, and manuscript integrity is untested.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Dedicated iterative scientific-literature discovery subsystem with explicit deep-search and wide-search objectives.
evidence: AutoResearchBench reports that even the strongest evaluated LLMs reach only 9.39% accuracy on Deep Research and 9.31% IoU on Wide Research, with many strong baselines below 5%.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: The benchmark establishes difficulty but does not yet identify a demonstrated high-performing mechanism.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Tournament/debate/evolve hypothesis generation with scaled test-time compute.
evidence: AI co-scientist evaluates 203 research goals and reports increasing self-evaluated Elo over iterative generate-debate-evolve computation: best-hypothesis Elo rises roughly from 1350 to 1610 and top-10 average from roughly 1250 to 1495 across ten temporal buckets.
The system also reports domain validations in drug repurposing, liver-fibrosis targets, and an independently rediscovered bacterial gene-transfer mechanism.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Hypothesis generation and biomedical co-science; Elo is self-evaluated rather than independent ground truth.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need independent matched-budget evaluation separating tournament evolution from model and compute scaling.

negative_and_boundary_evidence: Independent 2026 case studies tested eight open-source AI research frameworks on two real-world reproduction tasks; none completed the full research cycle, despite good planning/summarization, and the authors report sophisticated hallucinations plus heavy debugging requirements.

Nature reports only 1/3 AI Scientist submissions cleared a workshop bar, none met main-conference quality, and common failures include naive ideas, incorrect implementation, insufficient rigor, experimental errors, citation hallucinations, and duplicated figures.
ResearchClawBench's strongest autonomous agent averages 21.5 against a 50-point target-paper rediscovery threshold across 40 tasks/10 domains.
AIRS-Bench agents exceed human SOTA on only 4 of 20 tasks and fail to match it on 16, indicating that isolated wins should not be generalized to broad research autonomy.
AutoResearchBench shows scientific literature discovery remains unsolved even when general web-browsing benchmarks are much stronger.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Promote Agent Laboratory based mainly on its claimed 84% cost reduction and SOTA code performance.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Deferred: independent real-world evaluation reports failure to complete full research cycles and examples of fabricated results; need matched replication of its positive claims.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Treat workshop peer-review acceptance as sufficient scientific-validity evidence.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Rejected as a standalone signal: the accepted AI Scientist paper had approximately 57% train-test overlap found by internal code audit and external reviewers did not see the code.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Attribute AI Scientist-v2 gains specifically to tree search or VLM review.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Deferred: system changed multiple components at once and no clean component ablation was found; AIRS-Bench gives better scaffold-level evidence for tree search.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Use automated paper reviewer alone as a quality gate.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Insufficient: Nature reports automated-reviewer balanced accuracy comparable to human acceptance decisions, but code/data-integrity failures can remain invisible from the manuscript.

frontier: Inspect ASI-Bench methods/appendices to identify which agent scaffolds or planning structures retain performance when methodological guidance is withdrawn; extract per-domain and per-configuration failure patterns.
Extract matched per-model AIRS-Bench results (Greedy vs ReAct vs One-Shot), valid-submission rates, and compute budgets to isolate the causal contribution of parallel best-first search.
Read the full Pitfalls paper tables and released artifacts to quantify per-failure-mode prevalence and determine whether online audit interventions were tested or only post-hoc detection.
Inspect ResearchClawBench rubric/error taxonomy by agent to see whether protocol mismatch is primarily planning, execution, or evidence-grounding failure.
Cross-check Agent Laboratory's positive claims against its full evaluation tables and the independent 2026 reproduction study, preserving exact task/configuration differences.
Follow ASI-Bench citations for demonstrated method-selection or experiment-protocol planning mechanisms that close the large human-guidance gap.
Investigate whether Autodata-style outer-loop prompt/meta-optimization has been applied to end-to-end scientist agents rather than only data generation.
Search for PseudoBench follow-up interventions or premise-validation agents that improve resistance without collapsing legitimate exploratory science.

termination_diagnostics.additional_unresolved_frontier_action_be: After the initial autonomous-scientist/benchmark pass, branched into PseudoBench and Autodata to examine scientific-premise robustness and meta-optimized agentic data generation.
termination_diagnostics.stop_reason: Platform/runtime-bound scheduled run checkpoint, not research completion.

exact_next_action: Open ASI-Bench's full methods/results and AIRS-Bench's matched scaffold tables; extract per-agent/per-scaffold numbers that isolate method-selection and best-first-search effects before following citations into concrete planning mechanisms.
